router_body:
name: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: full job set selected
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
        run: echo 'SELECTED test samples render contents tier'
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
      - name: local gate wiring proof
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
        run: python3 -I ci/local-gate-test.py
      - name: local evidence gate
        if: ${{ !(github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix')) }}
        run: echo 'Local gauntlet evidence is the gate; request ci or full-matrix for CI.'

book.yml.test:
needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'test')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The hosts are the plan's (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): ubuntu, macOS and
        # windows in the full tier, ubuntu alone in a pull request's.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_test || '[]') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
      - name: fmt
        shell: bash
        run: cargo fmt --check
      - name: clippy
        shell: bash
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
      - name: tests
        shell: bash
        run: cargo test
      # Ruling #40 (wolf-book#43): EXERCISES-INDEX's tier column says which
      # machines executed each program, read off its `//! check:` head.
      # Generated by `cargo xtask tiers`; a hand-edited row fails here.
      # Reads the corpus only, so it needs no toolchain.
      - name: exercise index tiers are generated
        shell: bash
        run: cargo xtask tiers --check
      # bs62: chapter 7's memory diagrams are generated, so they are held
      # here without any toolchain: the text in each `memory` fence and the
      # SVG beside it are redrawn from the traces under snapshots/traces/
      # and must match byte for byte. (The samples lane re-takes the
      # traces themselves with the trace lupin.)
      - name: memory diagrams redraw from the checked-in traces
        shell: bash
        run: cargo xtask diagrams --check

  # Lane 2 — sample execution: build wolf (release, D57-stamped) and
  # lupin (release) at the wolf-toolchain.toml revs, run every sample,
  # then prove the rig catches deliberate breakage. 3-OS.
book.yml.samples:
needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'samples')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The hosts are the plan's (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): ubuntu, macOS and
        # windows in the full tier, ubuntu alone in a pull request's.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_samples || '[]') }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    # Stays 60. bs31 raised this to 90 on the theory that running every
    # `run(...)` sample under the compiler as well as the interpreter had
    # made the lane expensive. Measured on run 34319651351, it had not:
    # sample execution is 27s on ubuntu, 45s on windows, 75s on macOS,
    # and the whole job is 2-5 minutes against a 3-6 minute baseline.
    # The hour that got eaten was a hang, not work (a killed child's
    # grandchild held the pipes; see run_within), and a ceiling inflated
    # against a hang only makes the next one take longer to surface.
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: wolf-book
      - name: read pins
        id: pins
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book
        run: |
          rev() { awk -v s="[$1]" '$0==s{f=1} f&&/^rev = /{gsub(/"/,"",$3); print $3; exit}' wolf-toolchain.toml; }
          echo "wolf=$(rev wolf)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "lupin=$(rev lupin)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # The sibling repos are private; the default token cannot read them
      # (the is00 deploy-key lesson). Acquire tolerantly: with WOLF_CI_TOKEN
      # the lane runs in full; without it, every toolchain-dependent step
      # below skips LOUDLY (never vacuously green, never red on absence).
      - name: acquire pinned siblings
        id: acquire
        shell: bash
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.WOLF_CI_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          if [ -z "${TOKEN:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::WOLF_CI_TOKEN absent — sibling repos unreachable; samples lane skips (local runs remain the gate)"
            echo "toolchain=none" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          ok=1
          git clone --quiet "https://x-access-token:${TOKEN}@github.com/wolffe-lang/wolf-lang" wolf-lang \
            && git -C wolf-lang checkout --quiet "${{ steps.pins.outputs.wolf }}" || ok=0
          git clone --quiet "https://x-access-token:${TOKEN}@github.com/wolffe-lang/wolf-interp" wolf-interp \
            && git -C wolf-interp checkout --quiet "${{ steps.pins.outputs.lupin }}" || ok=0
          if [ "$ok" = 1 ]; then echo "toolchain=full" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else echo "::error::token present but sibling acquisition failed"; exit 1; fi
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: |
            wolf-book
            wolf-lang
            wolf-interp
      # `wolf build` links against the runtime staticlib and looks for it
      # beside the driver; the driver alone does not emit it, so the
      # native console blocks (ch01, ch09) need the wolf_rt target too.
      # The build is release-profile and carries the D57 stamp: the
      # book's version transcripts print the BARE release string, which
      # only a stamped build answers (an unstamped build says
      # `+dev.unknown` and claims nothing). The stamp is the same pair
      # `cargo xtask dist` computes — the commit, plus the release tag
      # exactly when one points at the pin — reproduced here because
      # dist's archive staging is not needed (and its windows staging
      # step fails at the v0.2.0 tag; fixed upstream at s60).
      #
      # `--short=7`, and the `=7` is load-bearing. A bare `--short` lets
      # git pick the width from the clone's object count, so the same
      # revision stamps `e0ce018` in a checkout that has sat on a box
      # for weeks and `e0ce0189` in a fresh clone — which is what this
      # runner makes. bs36 measured both, went green locally and red
      # here by one character in the `pin` clause, on two hosts. That is
      # wolf-lang#301, and `cargo xtask dist` now pins the width by
      # decision (`STAMP_SHA_WIDTH`). This step does not run `dist`, so
      # the decision does not reach it on its own: the two have to say
      # the same number, here, or the stamp is a coin flip on how many
      # objects the runner happened to fetch.
      - name: build pinned wolf (release, D57-stamped) + the runtime staticlib
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.toolchain == 'full'
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-lang
        run: |
          WOLF_COMMIT="$(git rev-parse --short=7 HEAD)"
          export WOLF_COMMIT
          WOLF_RELEASE="$(git tag --points-at HEAD | grep -E '^v[0-9]' | head -1 || true)"
          if [ -n "$WOLF_RELEASE" ]; then export WOLF_RELEASE; fi
          cargo build --release -p wolf_driver -p wolf_rt -p wolf_cimport
      # The release archive carries the standard library as `std/` beside
      # `wolf` (s204, ruling #59, since 0.2.27), and the driver's default
      # std root is that directory. A `cargo build` has nothing there, so
      # without this step the lane measured a toolchain no reader
      # installs: bs65 found `wolf interface` answering differently (ch22,
      # a std module reached through a method call joins the package's
      # interface and its hashes). Stage exactly what `cargo xtask dist`
      # stages: wolf-std's `std/` tree at the commit wolf-lang's
      # `crates/wolf_driver/STD-PIN` names, the two licences, and
      # `STD-REV`. The manifest below is the archive's own, measured from
      # the 0.2.36 release archive (r41q, docs/audit/r41q-evidence/;
      # wolf-std `78b9d3cb`, 59 files, manifest `f8a46216…`, the same from
      # a wolf-std checkout staged as this step stages it; 0.2.35's was
      # bs72's `fa26d724…`); a STD-PIN
      # bump moves it, and this step then fails until the bump re-measures it.
      # autocrlf off: windows runners convert line endings by default,
      # and the archive's bytes are LF.
      - name: stage std/ beside wolf, as the release archive does
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.toolchain == 'full'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sha() { if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null; then sha256sum "$@"; else shasum -a 256 "$@"; fi; }
          pin=$(awk -F' = ' '/^wolf-std-commit = /{print $2}' wolf-lang/crates/wolf_driver/STD-PIN)
          echo "STD-PIN: ${pin}"
          [ -n "${pin}" ]
          git -c core.autocrlf=false clone --quiet https://github.com/wolffe-lang/wolf-std wolf-std
          git -C wolf-std -c core.autocrlf=false checkout --quiet "${pin}"
          dest=wolf-lang/target/release/std
          rm -rf "${dest}"
          cp -R wolf-std/std "${dest}"
          cp wolf-std/LICENSE wolf-std/LICENSE-EXCEPTION "${dest}/"
          printf '%s\n' "${pin}" > "${dest}/STD-REV"
          # Each line written as `<hash>  <path>` by hand: windows' sha256sum
          # marks binary mode (`*path`), which would move the manifest and
          # nothing else.
          got=$(cd wolf-lang/target/release && find std -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | while IFS= read -r f; do printf '%s  %s\n' "$(sha "$f" | cut -c1-64)" "$f"; done | sha | cut -c1-64)
          want=f8a4621657b5234b9b2c6cb1795f35dc1e0387484d626b4ccf51e57b3c444fe9
          echo "staged std/: $(cd wolf-lang/target/release && find std -type f | wc -l) files, manifest ${got}"
          if [ "${got}" != "${want}" ]; then echo "::error::staged std/ manifest ${got} is not the 0.2.36 archive's ${want}"; exit 1; fi
      - name: build pinned lupin (release)
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.toolchain == 'full'
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-interp
        run: cargo build --release --bin lupin
      # The book's transcripts say `wolf build` prints nothing on its way
      # to a binary, and that is true when the toolchain finds the linker
      # it expects. Without `ld.lld` on PATH the driver notes the
      # substitution on stderr — real output, which a reader on a stock
      # linux box would see too — and the replay counts it as drift,
      # correctly (bs25: 19 of the first executing lane's failures were
      # this one line). Two ways out, and the book took this one: make
      # the lane match what ch01 §1.2 now tells the reader to install,
      # rather than teach the replay to delete a line of tool output.
      # The byte-compare stays a byte-compare. macOS links through
      # Apple's ld BY DESIGN (the automatic ad-hoc signature) and says
      # nothing; windows chooses its COFF linker by its own documented
      # order. So this is the linux lane's step alone.
      - name: lld, the linker the toolchain expects (linux)
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.toolchain == 'full' && runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y -qq lld
          # Loud, and fatal when absent: an lld that quietly failed to
          # install would put the driver's note back into 19 transcripts
          # and the lane would report it as book drift.
          command -v ld.lld
          ld.lld --version

      - name: run every sample
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.toolchain == 'full'
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book
        env:
          WOLF: ${{ github.workspace }}/wolf-lang/target/release/wolf${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '.exe' || '' }}
          LUPIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/wolf-interp/target/release/lupin${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '.exe' || '' }}
        run: cargo xtask samples
      - name: self-test (a deliberately-broken sample must fail)
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.toolchain == 'full'
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book
        env:
          WOLF: ${{ github.workspace }}/wolf-lang/target/release/wolf${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '.exe' || '' }}
          LUPIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/wolf-interp/target/release/lupin${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '.exe' || '' }}
        run: cargo xtask samples --self-test
      # bs62: the memory diagrams in chapter 7 are drawn from lupin's place
      # trace (`--trace-places`, wolf-interp is72). The trace lupin is the
      # rev in [lupin-trace]: the [lupin] pin itself when a release carries
      # the trace (then nothing extra is built), a source build of is72's
      # head until then. Its own target dir, so the pinned lupin the
      # samples ran is never rebuilt under them.
      - name: build the trace lupin ([lupin-trace])
        id: tracer
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.toolchain == 'full'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          rev() { awk -v s="[$1]" '$0==s{f=1} f&&/^rev = /{gsub(/"/,"",$3); print $3; exit}' wolf-book/wolf-toolchain.toml; }
          exe='${{ runner.os == 'Windows' && '.exe' || '' }}'
          t="$(rev lupin-trace)"; l="$(rev lupin)"
          if [ "$t" = "$l" ]; then
            echo "trace lupin = the pinned lupin ($l)"
            echo "lupin=${{ github.workspace }}/wolf-interp/target/release/lupin$exe" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "trace lupin = wolf-interp $t (the pinned lupin is $l)"
            git -C wolf-interp worktree add --detach ../wolf-interp-trace "$t"
            (cd wolf-interp-trace && cargo build --release --bin lupin)
            echo "lupin=${{ github.workspace }}/wolf-interp-trace/target/release/lupin$exe" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - name: memory diagrams re-taken from a fresh trace
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.toolchain == 'full'
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book
        env:
          LUPIN_TRACE: ${{ steps.tracer.outputs.lupin }}
        run: cargo xtask diagrams --check
      - name: doc truth
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book
        run: cargo xtask verify-docs
      # bs12: the audit-ledger gate. bs01's rule — "closing a chapter PR
      # requires its ledger emptied into issues or explicitly waived in
      # review" — is enforced here rather than aspirational: an open
      # `ba:*` row must cite wolf-lang#N or carry waived(...), and the
      # per-chapter counts land in the CI log instead of an HTML comment.
      - name: audit ledger (open rows filed or waived)
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book
        run: cargo xtask ledger --check
      - name: generated back matter is not stale
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book
        env:
          WOLF_LANG_PATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/wolf-lang
        run: cargo xtask backmatter --check
      # Contrast code rots too: the Rust the book prints in ch07 §7.6 is
      # vendored, compiled with warnings denied, asserted, and diffed
      # against the printed block. Runs without the wolf toolchain.
      - name: contrast code (other languages the book quotes)
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book
        run: cargo xtask contrast
      - name: corpus export artifact (sync PR input for wolf-lang corpus/book/)
        if: matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: corpus-book-export
          path: wolf-book/samples/export/corpus/book/
          retention-days: 14

  # Lane 3 — render: grammar drift against the wolf-lsp pin, then all
  # three artifacts. The PDF is required here — its absence fails the
  # build (DESIGN.md §4); typst comes from the release binary.
book.yml.render:
needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'render')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: wolf-book
      - name: read wolf-lsp pin
        id: pins
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book
        run: |
          rev() { awk -v s="[$1]" '$0==s{f=1} f&&/^rev = /{gsub(/"/,"",$3); print $3; exit}' wolf-toolchain.toml; }
          echo "lsp=$(rev wolf-lsp)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # wolf-lsp is private: the drift check runs only with WOLF_CI_TOKEN;
      # rendering always runs — the grammar is vendored in-repo.
      - name: acquire wolf-lsp for the drift check
        id: lsp
        shell: bash
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ secrets.WOLF_CI_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          if [ -z "${TOKEN:-}" ]; then
            echo "::notice::WOLF_CI_TOKEN absent — grammar drift check skips (vendored grammar still renders)"
            echo "have=none" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          git clone --quiet "https://x-access-token:${TOKEN}@github.com/wolffe-lang/wolf-lsp" wolf-lsp \
            && git -C wolf-lsp checkout --quiet "${{ steps.pins.outputs.lsp }}" \
            && echo "have=full" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" \
            || { echo "::error::token present but wolf-lsp acquisition failed"; exit 1; }
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: wolf-book
      - uses: typst-community/setup-typst@v4
      - name: grammar drift check (the book-side arrow)
        if: steps.lsp.outputs.have == 'full'
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book
        run: cargo xtask grammar-sync --check --lsp-path ../wolf-lsp
      - name: render web + wolf-book.md + wolf-book.pdf
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book
        run: cargo xtask render all --require-pdf
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wolf-book-artifacts
          path: |
            wolf-book/target/render/wolf-book.md
            wolf-book/target/render/wolf-book.pdf
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wolf-book-web
          path: wolf-book/target/render/web/
          retention-days: 14

  # Lane 4 — the contents (bs55). From every page of the render, click
  # every sidebar entry and hold the landing to its label: a page arrived
  # (HTTP 200, or 304 for a held copy the server confirmed, #67), the
  # label's name in <title>, the label's number in the <h1>. The render
  # is served under /book/ the way lupp.us serves it (serve.mjs: the
  # response headers of wolf-web nginx/lupp.us.conf:51-58 and :118,
  # revalidation with an ETag, and every script reference versioned
  # `?v=…`, wolf-boot.js included, #66), because the site's CSP is what a
  # reader's browser obeys and what GitHub Pages never sent: under
  # `script-src 'self'` no inline script runs, and the sidebar's links
  # 404ed from every page one directory down while a curl crawl and a
  # Pages run both saw nothing. Three engines, a 390px phone and a 1440px
  # desktop each; the sidebar's first-load state held to its drawing
  # with and without stored state.
book.yml.contents:
needs: [plan, render]
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'contents')
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        engine: [chromium, firefox, webkit]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: wolf-book
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wolf-book-web
          path: wolf-book/target/render/web
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: install playwright and ${{ matrix.engine }}
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book/tests/contents
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          npm install --no-audit --no-fund
          npx playwright install --with-deps ${{ matrix.engine }}
      - name: the gate's own tests
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book/tests/contents
        run: npm test
      - name: every sidebar entry from every page (${{ matrix.engine }}, phone + desktop)
        shell: bash
        working-directory: wolf-book/tests/contents
        run: node contents.mjs --root ../../target/render/web --engines ${{ matrix.engine }} --json contents-${{ matrix.engine }}.out.json
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: contents-${{ matrix.engine }}
          path: wolf-book/tests/contents/contents-${{ matrix.engine }}.out.json
          retention-days: 14

  # The run's verdict, and its name: `tier full`, `tier pr` or `tier noop`.
  # It needs every job, runs unless the run was cancelled, and fails unless
  # the plan succeeded, the jobs and hosts it chose are the tier's, every
  # chosen job succeeded and every other job was skipped (ci/tiers.py
  # verdict). lane-audit.sh reads this job's name and conclusion.
book.yml.tier:
name: tier ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tier || 'unplanned' }}
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    needs:
      - plan
      - test
      - samples
      - render
      - contents
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: every chosen job succeeded, every other was skipped
        env:
          NEEDS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: python3 ci/tiers.py verdict

  # A red nightly opens an issue (ruling #92): a scheduled run has no lane
  # watching it, so the red has to come and find one. One open issue per
  # workflow, its title the dedupe key; a further red night comments on it
  # (ci/nightly-red.sh, tested by ci/tiers-test.py T8). Never on a pull
  # request, a push or a dispatch: those reds have a lane attached already.
book.yml.nightly-red:
name: nightly red, an issue
    needs: tier
    if: ${{ failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: open or update the nightly-red issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          WORKFLOW: ${{ github.workflow }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: ci/nightly-red.sh
